description: Fig. 20 is a composite mechanism schematic (no axes, no scale bars, no printed numeric values anywhere) explaining how grain size controls oxide-film formation and corrosion in low-density steels (LDSs). It is organised as two stacked sequences, each made of a 3D grain-structure block, a 3D corroded-surface block, and a pair of 2D solution/metal cross-sections joined by a purple arrow; a blue curved arrow and a red vertical arrow separate the two sequences. (a) small grain size sample: a fine-grained block with a dense blue grain-boundary network and red ATBs; (a1) the same surface after attack, annotated "preferential dissolution" at blue aluminium-oxide particles on a pink film; (a2) cross-section with "preferential dissolution" arrows ejecting purple metal elements into the blue "Solution" containing orange chloridion spheres; (a3) a continuous, dense layer annotated "oxide film" made of aluminium oxide. (b) large grain size sample: coarser grains, sparser boundaries; (b1) corroded surface annotated "Crack" with mixed iron oxide (dark red) and manganese oxide (magenta); (b2) cross-section with no marked dissolution; (b3) discontinuous film with "crack" and "corrosion pit" labels and chloridion penetrating inward. Bottom legend: HAGBs, ATBs, metal elements, chloridion, aluminum oxide, iron oxide, manganese oxide. The figure argues fine grains/high boundary density yield a denser, more protective Al-rich film, whereas coarse grains give a cracked, pitted, multi-oxide film.

observations.observation: The figure is a two-part mechanism schematic (chart_schematic) with eight labelled sub-panels: (a), (a1), (a2), (a3) for the small-grain case and (b), (b1), (b2), (b3) for the large-grain case; no axes, scale bars or numeric values are printed.

The bottom legend defines: HAGBs (blue line), ATBs (red line), metal elements (purple sphere), chloridion (orange sphere), aluminum oxide (blue ellipse), iron oxide (dark-red ellipse), manganese oxide (magenta ellipse).
Panel (a) shows a fine-grained microstructure with a denser blue grain-boundary network and red ATB lines than the coarse-grained block in panel (b).
Panels (a1) and (a2) are annotated "preferential dissolution", with arrows showing purple metal elements leaving the metal surface into the solution.
Panel (a3) shows a continuous, laterally uniform layer annotated "oxide film" composed of aluminium oxide covering the metal, with no cracks or pits drawn.
Panel (b1) contains a label "Crack" pointing to a fissure in the surface oxide film of the coarse-grained sample.
Panel (b3) labels both "crack" and "corrosion pit" and depicts a discontinuous film containing aluminium oxide, iron oxide and manganese oxide markers.
Orange chloridion spheres are present in the solution in all four cross-section panels, and appear to reach the metal only in (b3).
The caption states that the figure shows oxide film formation and corrosion mechanisms of LDSs with different grain size, with (a) the small grain size sample and (b) the large grain size sample.
The citing text identifies the fine-grained case as the S950 sample, which has smaller grains and higher grain-boundary density, especially HAGBs and ATBs.

The citing text asserts that selective/preferential dissolution of metallic elements such as Al accelerates nucleation and growth of an Al-enriched oxide film, and that uniformly distributed ATBs promote homogeneous film formation.

The citing text claims the fine-grained sample ultimately yields a denser, more continuous protective layer; the pixels of (a3) versus (b3) are consistent with this (continuous versus cracked/pitted film).
No numeric value is printed on any panel of the figure; grain-size values (8.7-32 µm) come from the abstract/caption context, not from the image.

subfigures.description: 3D block diagram of the small grain size sample: a fine-grained metal block with a dense network of blue grain boundaries (HAGBs) and red lines (ATBs) on the top surface, and purple spheres (metal elements) decorating the boundaries.

3D block of the same fine-grained sample after corrosive attack: the top surface is covered by a pink oxide layer containing many blue ellipses (aluminium oxide); two arrows annotated "preferential dissolution" point to dissolution sites.

2D cross-section schematic: a blue "Solution" region containing orange chloridion spheres above a grey metal substrate with purple metal elements, blue HAGBs and red ATBs; two arrows labelled "preferential dissolution" show metal elements leaving the surface.

2D cross-section after film growth: a continuous, laterally uniform row of blue aluminium-oxide markers labelled "oxide film" covers the metal surface beneath the blue "Solution" with chloridion spheres.
3D block diagram of the large grain size sample: coarser grains with visibly fewer/simpler blue grain boundaries and red ATBs on the top surface, with purple metal elements.

3D block of the coarse-grained sample after attack: pink surface film containing blue aluminium oxide, dark-red iron oxide and magenta manganese oxide, with an arrow annotated "Crack" pointing to a fissure in the film.

2D cross-section schematic of the coarse-grained sample: blue "Solution" with orange chloridion spheres above a grey metal substrate containing a few blue HAGBs and red ATBs; no dissolution arrows are drawn.

2D cross-section after film formation: a discontinuous oxide film of mixed aluminium oxide (blue), iron oxide (dark red) and manganese oxide (magenta); arrows annotated "crack" and "corrosion pit" mark film breakdown, with chloridion spheres reaching the metal.
